panels.description: LynqNodes neither Ready nor failed: rolling out, recovering lost pods, or not created yet (including creation held back by maxSkew) (hub_desired - hub_ready - hub_failed). Not an error by itself; a rollout that stops progressing shows in Stalled Rollouts. Lynq v1.1.23-alpha.1 and earlier counted these nodes as failed, so this stays near 0 there.
panels.title: Progressing Nodes

panels.description: LynqNodes that need an operator: failed or conflicted resources, or Degraded=True. Nodes rolling out or recovering lost pods are not counted here (see Progressing Nodes), so Desired = Ready + Progressing + Failed. Lynq v1.1.23-alpha.1 and earlier counted every node with Ready!=True as failed.
panels.title: Total Failed Nodes

panels.description: LynqForms whose rollout phase is Failed (lynqform_rollout_phase == 2): an updated LynqNode failed, or did not become Ready within spec.rollout.progressDeadlineSeconds. The rollout stops; the stalled nodes are listed in the LynqForm's .status.rollout.message. Only LynqForms with spec.rollout.maxSkew > 0 report a rollout phase.
panels.title: Stalled Rollouts

panels.description: Only LynqNodes that are not Ready. Degraded=No means the node is progressing (rolling out or recovering lost pods) and needs no action yet; Degraded=Yes means failed or conflicted resources, or a template/variables/dependency error. Ready nodes are not listed.

targets.expr:
max by (lynqnode, namespace) (lynqnode_condition_status{type="Degraded"})
and on (lynqnode, namespace) (max by (lynqnode, namespace) (lynqnode_condition_status{type="Ready"}) != 1)

panels.title: Not-Ready LynqNodes (progressing vs degraded)

panels.description: LynqNodes with Degraded=True and the current reason. Not-ready alone (Ready=False/NotAllResourcesReady) never appears here; see Not-Ready LynqNodes.
panels.title: Degraded Nodes

panels.description: Failed = Lynq's own change never became Ready (readiness timeout, ProgressDeadlineExceeded) or failed to apply. A resource that was Ready and regressed (lost pod, drain, external rollout restart) is Not Ready, not Failed. Not Ready also includes resources skipped because a dependency failed (there is no skipped-resource metric). Desired = Ready + Not Ready + Failed.
panels.title: Resource Counts by Node

panels.description: Failed = Lynq's own change never became Ready (readiness timeout, ProgressDeadlineExceeded) or failed to apply. A resource that was Ready and regressed (lost pod, drain, external rollout restart) is Not Ready, not Failed. Not Ready also includes resources skipped because a dependency failed (there is no skipped-resource metric). Desired = Ready + Not Ready + Failed.
panels.title: Resource Counts (Total)

panels.description: Per hub: Desired = Ready + Progressing + Failed. Failed = LynqNodes needing an operator (failed or conflicted resources, or Degraded=True). Progressing = rolling out, recovering lost pods, or not created yet (including creation held back by maxSkew); not an error by itself. Lynq v1.1.23-alpha.1 and earlier counted progressing nodes as failed.

targets.expr: clamp_min(sum by (hub, namespace) (hub_desired) - sum by (hub, namespace) (hub_ready) - sum by (hub, namespace) (hub_failed), 0)

panels.title: Hub Node Breakdown

panels.description: Rollout phase per LynqForm (lynqform_rollout_phase: 0=Idle, 1=InProgress, 2=Failed, 3=Complete). Failed = an updated LynqNode failed, or did not become Ready within spec.rollout.progressDeadlineSeconds; it keeps its maxSkew slot, so the rollout stops. The stalled nodes are listed in kubectl get lynqform <name> -o jsonpath='{.status.rollout.message}'. Only LynqForms with spec.rollout.maxSkew > 0 report a rollout.
panels.title: LynqForm Rollout Phase

panels.description: Rollout progress (% of nodes Ready on the new LynqForm generation) and nodes currently updating (updated but not Ready; bounded by maxSkew). Progress that stays flat while Updating Nodes stays at maxSkew is a stalled rollout.
panels.title: LynqForm Rollout Progress
